title: Platform-Invariant Topic Modeling via Contrastive Learning to Mitigate Platform-Induced Bias
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2024
task: Topic modelling over posts aggregated from several social platforms
problem: Platform-specific style and jargon bias topic models when documents from several platforms are pooled.
architecture: PITopic: a fixed pretrained language-model backbone encodes posts; a shallow network maps them to K-dimensional topic embeddings; platform-invariant contrastive learning pulls together semantically similar posts across platforms; platform-specific jargon word sets are removed before topic-word extraction.

datasets.name: Real-world data (X, Reddit, YouTube)
datasets.details: 250,000 English posts per platform, December 2022 - March 2023 (1.5 million collected)

datasets.name: Synthetic data (20NewsGroup, BBC, NYT)
datasets.details: 20NewsGroup, BBC and The New York Times as sources

metrics: mutual information between topics and platforms (lower is better)
key_results: Real data: mutual information with platform 0.032 vs 0.073 for BERTopic and 0.097 for LDA; average NPMI 0.529 vs 0.339 for BERTopic.
A RoBERTa classifier identifies the platform of a post with 96% accuracy, showing strong platform signatures.
strengths: Explicitly measures and reduces platform bias; tested on real and synthetic multi-source data.

limitations.text: No rule of thumb for the size of the jargon list; fixed backbone; one real-world keyword case study.
Topics independent of platforms may miss platform-specific opinions.
